text:
maya: Heads up — after the canary for hybrid-routing we saw a tail latency regression on the 8xA100 pool. Looks tied to multi-variant compat fallback.

maya: Symptoms: p95 went from ~120ms to ~230ms for short-chat workloads, throughput steady-ish but batches are much smaller. Token cost per request up ~12%. KV cache hit-rate dropped ~18% on the same hosts. :eyes:

tony: Interesting. Any profiler traces? kernel selection mismatch?

maya: Yes — attached a short snippet from the scheduler trace (copied):

```
SCHED: batch_formed size=3 wait_time=6ms compat_set=[v1-small, v2-quant]
KERNEL: selected=fp16_generic expected=quant_int4
KV: eviction_count=42 warmup_latency_ms=9
REQUEST: token_budget=64 actual_tokens=82 -> split into 2 fragments
```

maya: So requests are getting split (token budget exceeded), forming tiny batches and sometimes routing to a fallback variant that chooses a non-quant kernel. Kernel switch + extra KV misses looks like the culprit.

liam: That matches what I saw in profiling — the compat_set matching is too permissive, causing some v2-quant requests to fall back into v1-small buckets that have kernels optimized for different dims. The scheduler then can't coalesce kernels so we get mixed-kernel batches -> force fallback to safer kernel.

eva: Where is token_budget coming from? Is it per-queue or per-variant? We set target 64 tokens for latency SLO, but some prompts have system+context spikes.

tony: token_budget is computed per-queue based on median seq length + safety margin. But multi-variant routing currently uses a shared queue for compat sets; that means a single queue's token budget is applied even when variant widths diverge.

tony: Quick root-cause hypothesis: compat-set grouping + shared queue -> token budget mismatches -> batch fragmentation -> kernel selection fallback -> KV cache churn (different variant keys) -> tail latency regression.

maya: Agreed. I also ran a kernel-level microbenchmark: mixing seq-length distributions increases kernel setup overhead by ~30% because of memcpy/format conversions.

liam: Proposed mitigations:
- tighten compat sets (no mixing quant variants with fp variants unless kernel equivalence proven)
- compute token_budget per-variant or per-subqueue instead of per-compat-queue
- add a short batching wait (2-4ms) for small fragments to allow coalescing, but only for low-latency-insensitive customers
- KV prefetch for predicted fallback targets (warm up KV on canary)

eva: Prefetch sounds risky for memory but might pay off. We should simulate KV pressure: can we replay production traces against the canary with toggles?

maya: I ran a 6-hour replay with 10% traffic and a toggle for per-variant token budgets. Results: p95 improved back to ~130ms, KV hit-rate recovered to within 3% of baseline, cost slightly up due to more batching padding.

tony: Nice. Any regression on throughput?

maya: Throughput stable; CPU on host increased +6% due to extra batching logic, but within headroom.

liam: Next steps I recommend:
1) short term: enable per-variant subqueues for compat sets + conservative tighten of compat membership (feature flag).
2) medium: expose token_budget tunables per-customer in console + auto-tune based on observed seq histogram.
3) long term: kernel fingerprinting — if two variants produce identical kernel execution plan, allow merging; otherwise keep separate queues.

eva: Also add metrics to Console: compat_set_mismatch_rate, kernel_switch_rate, kv_eviction_rate tied to queue_id. Set alerts if mismatch_rate > 2% for >5m.

maya: I'll open a PR for the feature flag toggle and the per-variant subqueue tonight (small change in scheduler).

infra-bot: deploy-canary started for toggles/variant-subqueue at canary-2026-03-18-01 :rocket:

tony: Thanks — once canary hits 1h stable with p95 within 10% of baseline we can roll to prod. Also let's run an A/B with kernel-fingerprint disabled vs enabled.

liam: I'll prepare a replay bucket with the mixed-seqlen traces and a kv-warmup script.

maya: Logging action items:
- maya: PR for toggle/subqueue + canary (today)
- liam: replay traces + KV warmup script (today)
- eva: add Console metrics/alerts (this sprint)
- tony: plan A/B for kernel-fingerprint (next week)

maya: Thanks team. Short-term fix should remove the most painful tail regressions. We'll monitor for any cost regressions. :thumbsup:
